_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 21 (Isaac's birth; Hagar/Ishmael expelled; Beer-Sheba covenant). Saadia-specific moves: v.6 'סרורא' = 'joy' (renders צחק 'laughter' as 'joy'); v.20 'נער ראם' = 'a youth, an archer' (Saadia explicit for רובה קשת); v.33 'רב אלעאלם / אלאהי אלעאלם' = 'Lord of the world' / 'God of eternity' (Saadia treats 'אל עולם' as a divine attribute: master of the world / eternal God).

translations.1: Then God remembered Sarah, as He had said; and He did for her as He had promised.
translations.2: And she conceived, and bore to Abraham a son in his old age — at the time which God had spoken.
translations.3: And Abraham named his son who was born to him — whom Sarah bore to him — Isaac.
translations.4: And he circumcised him at eight days old, as God had commanded him.
translations.5: And Abraham was a son of a hundred years when Isaac his son was born to him.
translations.6: And Sarah said: 'God has made joy for me — everyone who hears will rejoice with me.'
translations.7: Then she said: 'Whoever said to Abraham that Sarah should nurse children — has spoken true; for I have borne him a son in his old age.'
translations.8: Then the boy grew, and was weaned; and Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
translations.9: Then Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, playing.
translations.11: And the matter was very hard on Abraham, on account of his son.
translations.12: And God said to him: 'Let not the matter be hard upon you concerning the boy and your maidservant. Everything that Sarah says to you — accept it from her; for through Isaac shall your offspring be named.
translations.13: And the son of the maidservant also — I shall make of him a nation, for he is your offspring.'
translations.14: And Abraham rose early in the morning; and he took food and a waterskin, and gave it to Hagar, setting it upon her shoulder; and he gave her the boy, and sent her away. And she went, and wandered, in the wilderness of Beer-Sheba.
translations.15: And the water in the skin was used up; and she cast the boy under one of the trees.
translations.16: And she went, and sat opposite him, at a distance as far as a bowshot — for she said: 'Let me not see the death of the boy.' And she sat opposite him, and lifted up her voice, and wept.
translations.17: And God heard the voice of the boy; and the angel of God called to Hagar from the sky, and said to her: 'What troubles you, O Hagar? Fear not — for God has heard the voice of the boy, where he is.
translations.18: Arise, lift him up, and strengthen your hand upon him — for I shall make of him a great nation.'
translations.19: And God uncovered her sight, and she saw a well of water. And she went, and filled the skin with water, and gave the boy to drink.
translations.20: And God was with him until he grew up; and he settled in the wilderness, and was a youth, an archer.
translations.21: And he settled in the wilderness of Paran; and his mother took for him a wife from the land of Egypt.
translations.22: And it was at that time that Abimelech, and Phicol the chief of his army, said to Abraham: 'God is with you in all that you do.
translations.23: Now swear to me here by God, that you shall not betray me, nor my offspring, nor my posterity. According to the kindness which I have done with you — shall you do with me, and with the land in which you have sojourned.'
translations.25: And Abraham reproved Abimelech, on account of the well of water which the servants of Abimelech had seized by force.
translations.26: Abimelech said: 'I do not know who did this thing; and you did not tell me; and I, too, have not heard of it — except today.'
translations.27: And Abraham took sheep and cattle, and gave them to Abimelech; and the two of them made a covenant.
translations.28: And Abraham set aside seven ewes of the flock by themselves.
translations.29: Abimelech said to him: 'What are these seven ewes which you have set apart by themselves?'
translations.30: He said: 'That you shall take them from my hand — that they may be a witness for me that I have dug this well.'
translations.31: Therefore the place was called Beer-Sheba — for there the two of them swore.
translations.32: And when they had made the covenant in Beer-Sheba, Abimelech and Phicol the chief of his army arose, and returned to the land of the Philistines.
translations.33: And he set up a marker in Beer-Sheba, and called there upon the name of God, the Lord of the World.
translations.34: Then Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines for a long time.
